plan.goal: Add unit tests for the notifications module and the admin module, and document the exported types in the TypeScript client.
plan.rationale: The repository currently has tests for auth, orders, and users, but no tests for notifications or admin. The TypeScript client exports types, but those exports are not documented. Adding pytest coverage for the Python modules and JSDoc documentation for client exports will improve reliability and maintainability.

results.notes:
Created tests/test_notifications.py via cursor-agent with pytest tests for src/notifications.py. Coverage includes success returns, INFO logging via caplog, empty-string edge cases, None arguments, unicode/special characters, long message bodies, and logger failure propagation using monkeypatch. No changes were made to src/notifications.py or other files. Note: git_diff returned an empty diff, likely because tests/test_notifications.py is a new untracked file; cursor-agent reported tests/test_notifications.py as the only changed file. Intended file content:

from src.notifications import send_email, send_sms
import logging
import pytest


def test_send_email_returns_true():
    result = send_email("user@example.com", "Welcome", "Thanks for signing up")
    assert result is True


def test_send_sms_returns_true():
    result = send_sms("+15551234567", "Your verification code is 1234")
    assert result is True


def test_send_email_logs_info_message(caplog):
    with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO, logger="src.notifications"):
        send_email("user@example.com", "Welcome", "Thanks for signing up")

    assert "Sending email to user@example.com: Welcome" in caplog.text
    assert caplog.records[0].levelno == logging.INFO


def test_send_sms_logs_info_message(caplog):
    with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO, logger="src.notifications"):
        send_sms("+15551234567", "Your verification code is 1234")

    assert "Sending SMS to +15551234567: Your verification code is 1234" in caplog.text
    assert caplog.records[0].levelno == logging.INFO


def test_send_email_accepts_empty_strings():
    result = send_email("", "", "")
    assert result is True


def test_send_sms_accepts_empty_strings():
    result = send_sms("", "")
    assert result is True


def test_send_email_accepts_none_values():
    result = send_email(None, None, None)
    assert result is True


def test_send_sms_accepts_none_values():
    result = send_sms(None, None)
    assert result is True


def test_send_email_handles_unicode_and_special_characters():
    result = send_email(
        "üser@example.com",
        "Héllo — 通知",
        "Line one\nLine two\twith tab & <tags> \"quotes\"",
    )
    assert result is True


def test_send_sms_handles_unicode_and_special_characters():
    result = send_sms("+1 (555) 123-4567", "Héllo — 通知\nSecond line")
    assert result is True


def test_send_email_handles_long_body():
    body = "x" * 100_000
    result = send_email("user@example.com", "Long message", body)
    assert result is True


def test_send_sms_handles_long_message():
    message = "y" * 100_000
    result = send_sms("+15551234567", message)
    assert result is True


def test_send_email_propagates_logger_failure(monkeypatch):
    def failing_info(*args, **kwargs):
        raise RuntimeError("logger failed")

    monkeypatch.setattr("src.notifications.logger.info", failing_info)

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="logger failed"):
        send_email("user@example.com"

cursor_code was called once and edited only the two allowed files (src/client/types.ts, src/client/index.ts); git_diff confirms documentation-only changes with no runtime or type-semantic modifications.

src/client/types.ts — every exported interface now has a block JSDoc summary plus per-property `/** ... */` comments:
- CreateOrderRequest (userId, token, items, quantity)
- Order (id, status, userId, items, quantity)
- ChargeRequest (userId, token, amount, currency — optionality noted as server default)
- ChargeResult (id, status, amount, currency)
- LoginRequest (email, password)
- Session (token, userId)

src/client/index.ts — each re-exported type name in the `export type { ... } from "./types.ts"` block received a one-line JSDoc summary matching the types.ts descriptions; export order, quote style, and semicolons preserved. No `export *` existed, so no wildcard handling was needed.

Caveats / not fully satisfied (single cursor_code call limit reached, so these could not be corrected):
1. Rule 7 asked for a file-level JSDoc at the top of index.ts describing it as the public entry point, and a single statement-level comment above the type re-export instead of per-symbol comments. The current diff has the per-symbol one-liners but is missing the file-level header and the consolidated statement-level comment.
2. No exported enums, union/literal aliases, generic type parameters, or function-type aliases exist in types.ts, so `@template`, `@param`/`@returns`, discriminant-value lists, and `@deprecated` tags were not applicable and were not added.
3. No build/typecheck was run; edits are comment-only and syntactically well-formed.
